name: CDM — chemically defined medium for Lactobacillaceae
description: Chemically defined medium that supports growth of the whole Lactobacillaceae family. Glucose plus acetate and citrate, all 20 amino acids, the nucleobase/nucleoside set (uracil, guanine, adenine, xanthine, inosine, orotate, thymidine) and the B-vitamins. Exchange constraints as published in Table 2 of Ardalani et al. (mSystems 2024). Inorganic ions and water are opened, as they were left unconstrained in the paper's FBA setup.

provenance.citation: Ardalani O., Phaneuf P.V., Mohite O.S., Nielsen L.K. Pangenome reconstruction of Lactobacillaceae metabolism predicts species-specific metabolic traits. mSystems 9(7):e00156-24 (2024), Table 2.
provenance.notes: Ids are given in the pre-2018 BiGG convention (EX_glc_D_e, EX_arg_L_e), matching LactoPanGEM. Four labels in the published table disagreed with their BiGG id and are corrected here to the id: EX_ura_e is uracil (not uridine), EX_gua_e is guanine (not guanosine), EX_ade_e is adenine (not adenosine), and EX_nac_e is nicotinate/niacin (not N-acetyl-D-glucosamine, which is EX_acgam_e). The ids are unchanged.

composition_provenance.definition: sourced = the cited source states this component; derived = the pipeline supplied it. Classification table: tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv.

coverage_source.definition: pct_covered_all = components / (components + unresolved ingredients) — the legacy metric, which counts pipeline-derived components as covered. pct_covered_source = source-stated components / (those + unresolved ingredients + ingredients replaced by derived components). Component classes come from tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv. A null value means the denominator was zero; it does not mean 100.
